requirements.text: Treat “Motivating Reset” and “Designed to De-Stress” as strategic intent, not proof that a specific product relieves stress or produces health outcomes.
Use health, medical, physiological, quantified-performance, or recovery claims only with current, approved, product-specific substantiation.
Do not present the Visual World Guide as approved or turn its draft examples, proposed rules, or scorecard into binding brand standards.

preferences.text: Draft and research proposals favor contemporary, usable domestic spaces, tactile materials, natural or credible practical light, and room for everyday connection. Treat these as exploratory direction, not approved specifications.
Draft creative direction favors believable rest, reading, conversation, and readiness over presenter poses or forced excitement; this is proposed art direction, not an approved casting standard.
Supplied official-site material shows a red symbol and uppercase DUROFLEX wordmark. This is an observed identity pattern; confirm approved production artwork rather than reconstructing it.
Collected official-site examples include promotional, domestic, and technology-led treatments. They document dated practice, not a unified or mandatory visual system.

preserve: Keep the supplied strategic essence and public philosophy attributed as brand intentions, not product-performance evidence.
Preserve the selected product’s authentic appearance and branding; reference interiors are inspiration, not verified product assets.
Keep the draft status of the Visual World Guide visible when drawing on its ideas.
explore: Explore domestic settings that make space for both pause and renewed participation.
Use the draft’s spatial, material, lighting, and human-direction ideas as hypotheses; validate identity, product accuracy, and claims separately.
Develop category-specific treatments around the confirmed SKU rather than imposing one palette or setting across the range.
avoid: Do not imply medical benefit, stress treatment, or product efficacy from positioning language, a pose, or a reference image.
Do not treat draft typography, logo renderings, colour examples, or conflicting red-use examples as approved standards.
Do not assume proposed portfolio names or draft taglines are adopted, or borrow another brand’s visual identity.
unknowns: Approved production logo, lockup, tagline, and typography remain unresolved.
The Visual World Guide is draft material; final adoption of its visual direction is not established.
No SKU, campaign, channel, approved claim set, or offer has been selected for this reusable context.
Adoption of the proposed portfolio architecture is not established.
guide.decisionSummary: Use Duroflex’s supplied positioning as strategic context and retain its stated draft authority. No mandatory visual execution rules are established here. Treat visual directions and observed website patterns as preferences or proposals, confirm production identity, and require product-specific substantiation for claims.
